answer: Cross-epoch pulse matching. Each identity must emit a periodic heartbeat whose timing and payload derive from a slowly rotating saffron seed known only to the agent. During the next tide, verifiers replay past pulses against the current seed: genuine agents inherit a consistent trajectory, while clones built after the seed rotates carry none. An attacker must reconstruct every identity's full pulse history before each rotation, paying continuous compute and storage per clone rather than a one-time fee.
